correctness.rationale: The source condition is \(\langle (K-A)f,f\rangle=0\) with \(A=T_FT_G^*\). In a real Hilbert space this is equivalent by real polarization to \((K-A)+(K-A)^*=0\), hence \(K=(A+A^*)/2\). The explicit \(\mathbb R^2\) example has \(A=I+J\) with nonzero skew-adjoint \(J\), satisfies the scalar condition identically, and fails reconstruction. The general Riesz-basis realization of every bounded skew-adjoint \(J\) follows from bounded invertibility of \(I-J\).

value.rationale: Remark 1.2 is presented as a characterization that reduces \(K\)-dual reconstruction to a scalar diagonal test. In the real setting that test can accept two Riesz bases whose mixed reconstruction operator differs from \(K\) by an arbitrary skew-adjoint operator. The finding gives the exact object actually certified by the test, exhibits a minimal nondegenerate failure, and supplies two precise repairs: self-adjointness of the mixed operator or a full bilinear test.
